lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: line plots with fractional data

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

items.prompt: A rectangular prism is 2 unit cubes long, 3 wide, and 4 high. How many unit cubes fill it?

steps: One layer on the base holds 2 × 3 = 6 cubes.
The prism is 4 layers tall, so it holds 4 copies of that layer: 6 × 4 = 24 cubes.
Counting cubes measures volume, so the answer is 24 cubic units — the base alone, 6 square units, is only one layer.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Find the volume of a rectangular prism with length 5, width 7, and height 6 units.
An L-shaped solid is decomposed into two non-congruent rectangular prisms sharing a base of 6 by 6 units and having heights 7 and 2 units. What is its combined volume?
A storage box is 5 inches by 2 inches by 3 inches. What is its capacity?
A line plot has 2 marks at 1/4 meter, 5 marks at 1/2 meter, and 4 marks at 3/4 meter. What total length do the marks represent?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: A rectangular prism is 3 unit cubes long, 5 wide, and 8 high. How many unit cubes fill it?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Find the volume of a rectangular prism with length 6, width 3, and height 6 units.

items.prompt: An L-shaped solid is decomposed into two non-congruent rectangular prisms sharing a base of 6 by 7 units and having heights 4 and 6 units. What is its combined volume?
